# Lists and tables

From [the component index](../components.md). A prop with `?` is optional, and `= x` is its default. An indented line is the shape of a value the prop takes. In the examples, `children`, `transactions`, the icons and the handlers stand for the screen's own content, data and state.

## List, ListRow

```tsx
import { List } from "@tuja/ui/components/list";
import { ListRow } from "@tuja/ui/components/list-row";
```

Rows that each open something, such as transactions or accounts: a name, a detail line, a value and a caret.

### List

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<ul>`):

- `children: ReactNode` — The rows, each a `ListRow`.
- `form?: "card" | "plain" = "card"` — `card` puts the rows on a bordered surface with a divider between them.
- `density?: "regular" | "compact" = "regular"` — `compact` sets the rows in smaller type, for a dense list such as the sidebar of a `NavigationSplitView`: the name in body-small, the detail line in caption.

### ListRow

Props (also `css`):

- `children: ReactNode` — The row's name, on one line unless the row sets `wrap`.
- `wrap?: boolean = false` — Lets the name and the detail line wrap onto more lines instead of ending in an ellipsis, and breaks a long word such as an e-mail address.
- `detail?: ReactNode` — A muted line under the name, such as a summary or a count.
- `extra?: ReactNode` — More lines under the detail line, such as a line of Badges or a note.
- `leading?: ReactNode` — Shown before the name, such as an Avatar, an icon or an emoji.
- `leadingSize?: "sm" | "md" | "lg"` — Puts `leading` in a square box of this size, so the names of all rows start on one line.
- `leadingShape?: "circle" | "square"` — Draws a sunken plate of this shape behind `leading`.
- `value?: ReactNode` — The main figure of the row, such as an amount, at the end of the top line.
- `valueDetail?: ReactNode` — A muted line under `value`, such as a balance or a converted amount.
- `trailing?: ReactNode` — Shown at the end, before the caret, such as a Badge.
- `below?: ReactNode` — Content under the row, outside the part that opens it, that starts where the name starts, such as a `Select` that picks a category in place.
- `actions?: ReactNode` — Buttons after the row, outside the part that opens it, such as "Move up".
- `caret?: boolean = true` — Shows the caret that says the row opens something.
- `aria-current?: AriaAttributes["aria-current"]` — Marks the row that is open.
- `ref?: Ref<HTMLElement>` — Ref to the link or button.
- `href?: string | never` — Where the row goes.
- `linkComponent?: ComponentType<ListRowLinkProps> | never` — The component that renders the link, such as a router's link.
- `onClick?: never | (() => void)` — What the row does when pressed.
- `aria-pressed?: boolean` — Makes the button a toggle that is on or off, such as a row that picks a filter.

Example:

```tsx
function ListExample() {
  return (
    <List>
      {transactions.map((transaction) => (
        <ListRow
          key={transaction.id}
          href={`/transactions/${transaction.id}`}
          leading={<ShoppingCartIcon weight="bold" />}
          leadingShape="circle"
          detail={
            <MetaLine
              facts={[
                transaction.category ?? "Needs a category",
                transaction.account,
              ]}
            />
          }
          value={transaction.amount}
        >
          {transaction.payee}
        </ListRow>
      ))}
    </List>
  );
}
```

Example:

```tsx
function ListRowExample() {
  return (
    <ListRow
      onClick={close}
      value="−£4.20"
      below={
        <Select
          label="Category"
          labelHidden
          size="sm"
          placeholder="Choose a category"
          options={CATEGORIES}
        />
      }
    >
      SQ *BLANK STREET
    </ListRow>
  );
}
```

## Table, TableHead, TableBody, TableFoot, TableRow, TableHeaderCell, TableCell

```tsx
import { Table } from "@tuja/ui/components/table";
import { TableHead } from "@tuja/ui/components/table-head";
import { TableBody } from "@tuja/ui/components/table-body";
import { TableFoot } from "@tuja/ui/components/table-foot";
import { TableRow } from "@tuja/ui/components/table-row";
import { TableHeaderCell } from "@tuja/ui/components/table-header-cell";
import { TableCell } from "@tuja/ui/components/table-cell";
```

A static data table with columns to compare; not a data grid.

### Table

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<table>`):

- `children: ReactNode` — The table's groups — `TableHead`, `TableBody`, `TableFoot`.
- `caption: string` — Names the table and its scroll region.
- `captionVisible?: boolean = false` — Renders the `caption` above the table.
- `stickyHeader?: boolean = false` — Holds `TableHead` at the top of the scroll container while the rows move under it.
- `stickyColumn?: boolean = false` — Holds the first column at the start edge while the other columns scroll sideways under it, so each row keeps its label in view.
- `verticalAlign?: "top" | "middle" = "top"` — Where each cell sets its content in the height of its row.
- `containerCss?: StyleProp` — StyleX overrides for the scroll region's root, composed last — where a height or a width cap goes.
- `contentCss?: StyleProp` — StyleX styles merged over the scroller in the scroll region — inline padding that keeps the table off the region's edges, for a region that sits flush against its container's edge so the rows blur out there.

### TableHead

Props: `css`, and every attribute of `<thead>`.

### TableBody

Props: `css`, and every attribute of `<tbody>`.

### TableFoot

Props: `css`, and every attribute of `<tfoot>`.

### TableRow

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<tr>`):

- `current?: boolean = false` — Marks the row the visitor is on, pairing the tint with heavier type so the state survives a colour-blind or forced-colours read.
- `intent?: "warning" | "danger"` — Tints the row in the colour of an Intent.

### TableHeaderCell

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<th>`):

- `align?: "start" | "center" | "end" = "start"` — Text alignment. `numeric` end-aligns the cell on its own, and an explicit `align` beats it.
- `numeric?: boolean = false` — Renders figures at a fixed width and end-aligns the cell, so a column of numbers lines up digit for digit.
- `scope: "col" | "row" | "colgroup" | "rowgroup"` — Which cells this header labels: `"col"` for a column header in the head, `"row"` for the label at the start of a body row.

### TableCell

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<td>`):

- `align?: "start" | "center" | "end" = "start"` — Text alignment. `numeric` end-aligns the cell on its own, and an explicit `align` beats it.
- `numeric?: boolean = false` — Renders figures at a fixed width and end-aligns the cell, so a column of numbers lines up digit for digit.

Example:

```tsx
function TableExample() {
  return (
    <Table caption="Transactions" stickyHeader>
      <TableHead>
        <TableRow>
          <TableHeaderCell scope="col">Payee</TableHeaderCell>
          <TableHeaderCell scope="col" numeric>
            Amount
          </TableHeaderCell>
        </TableRow>
      </TableHead>
      <TableBody>
        {transactions.map((transaction) => (
          <TableRow key={transaction.id}>
            <TableHeaderCell scope="row">{transaction.payee}</TableHeaderCell>
            <TableCell numeric>{transaction.amount}</TableCell>
          </TableRow>
        ))}
      </TableBody>
    </Table>
  );
}
```

## TableDisclosure, TableDisclosureTrigger

```tsx
import { TableDisclosure } from "@tuja/ui/components/table-disclosure";
import { TableDisclosureTrigger } from "@tuja/ui/components/table-disclosure-trigger";
```

A table row that opens a panel under it; use it in place of `TableBody`, one per row.

### TableDisclosure

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<tr>`):

- `children: ReactNode` — Panel content. The panel spans the row under the summary, and stays as wide as the visible part of a table that scrolls sideways.
- `summary: ReactNode` — The cells of the row that opens and closes the panel, each one a `TableHeaderCell` or a `TableCell`.
- `panelCss?: StyleProp` — StyleX styles merged over the panel's box: its padding and the layout of its content.
- `open?: boolean` — Controlled open state. Omit to let the component own it.
- `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void` — Called with the next state whenever the row toggles.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean = false` — Initial open state when uncontrolled.

### TableDisclosureTrigger

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<button>`):

- `children: ReactNode` — The button's text, which is also its accessible name, such as the label of the row.

## MetaLine

```tsx
import { MetaLine } from "@tuja/ui/components/meta-line";
```

Facts on one line with a "·" between them, such as the detail line of a row.

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<span>`):

- `facts: readonly ReactNode[]` — The facts in order: text, a `Badge`, a link, or another `MetaLine` to keep a group of facts together.

Example:

```tsx
function MetaLineExample() {
  return (
    <MetaLine
      facts={[
        "Groceries",
        "Monzo Current",
        <Badge key="pending" size="sm">
          Pending
        </Badge>,
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Badge

```tsx
import { Badge } from "@tuja/ui/components/badge";
```

A short status or label, such as Pending or Overdue.

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<span>`):

- `children: ReactNode` — Badge contents — usually a short label.
- `intent?: "default" | "neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "accent" = "default"` — Which colour the badge carries.
- `size?: "sm" | "md" = "md"` — Padding scale. Both sizes set the text in the `caption` type role.
- `icon?: ReactNode` — Optional leading icon, rendered decoratively (`aria-hidden`).

Example:

```tsx
function BadgeExample() {
  return (
    <Badge intent="warning" size="sm">
      Overdue
    </Badge>
  );
}
```

## StatusDot

```tsx
import { StatusDot } from "@tuja/ui/components/status-dot";
```

A small dot that says something waits, beside a label or on an icon.

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<span>`):

- `intent: "neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "accent"` — Which colour the dot carries, from the same Intents as `Badge`.
- `label?: ReactNode` — What the dot means, read by a screen reader and not shown.

## Avatar

```tsx
import { Avatar } from "@tuja/ui/components/avatar";
```

A person or organisation: portrait, logo or monogram.

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<span>`):

- `name: string` — Who the avatar stands for, and the source of the derived monogram when there is no `src` or `initials`.
- `src?: string` — Portrait layered over the monogram, rendered decoratively since the root already carries the accessible name.
- `initials?: string` — Overrides the derived monogram, e.g. when the derivation picks the wrong characters or two would crowd.
- `size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" = "md"` — Diameter and type scale, in rem so the medallion scales with the user's font size.
- `shape?: "circle" | "square" = "circle"` — `"circle"` (the default) is for a person.
- `look?: "subtle" | "solid" = "subtle"` — `"subtle"` (the default) is a quiet tinted medallion for anyone present.
- `badge?: ReactNode` — Corner marker on its own surface — a status dot, a small icon.
- `badgeLabel?: string` — What the badge means, appended to the avatar's accessible name — the package ships no i18n, so the consumer supplies the localised string.
